source_policy: Definitions are original paraphrases of first-party DreamCo material; external reference section was excluded.

terms.definition: A deterministic procedure that converts text into a sequence of discrete units and can reconstruct the original text when the encoding is lossless.
A representation that begins with the 256 possible byte values and can therefore represent every valid UTF-8 byte sequence.
A Unicode text encoding in which a string is represented as a sequence of bytes; the trainer consumes these bytes directly.
An explicit transformation of text representation; NFC and NFKC can change code-point sequences and therefore must not be applied silently.
A boundary-setting step applied before subword learning or segmentation.
A subword method that repeatedly merges frequent adjacent symbols or byte tokens into larger vocabulary entries.
One recorded BPE rule joining a selected left token and right token into their concatenated token.
The available token inventory; in this trainer it consists of all 256 byte tokens plus learned merge tokens.
The correctness property that decoding an encoded input reproduces the exact original string.
The ability to represent every byte in the input; a full 256-byte base vocabulary gives complete byte coverage for valid UTF-8 strings.
The fraction of input units that cannot be represented by the vocabulary; a byte-level base vocabulary can avoid unknown bytes for valid UTF-8.
The number of produced tokens per word or other chosen text unit; lower values can reduce sequence length but must be balanced against vocabulary cost.
A measure such as bytes per token that indicates how compactly a tokenizer represents text.
The increase or decrease in token sequence length relative to the input text representation; it affects downstream context and compute.
A reserved token such as a beginning/end marker or role/tool marker that must remain atomic and have a stable ID.
A mapping from token positions back to source-text spans; the current byte-BPE trainer does not implement this feature.
An isolated evaluation split that must not be used for fitting, vocabulary construction, or model selection.
A traceable record that authorizes a source for a specific purpose; public visibility alone is not permission.
The source identity, version, owner/scope, content hash, transformation record, and permission history attached to an artifact.
The requirement that tokenizer vocabulary, special-token map, revision, and model checkpoint interface match exactly.
A separate neural training activity that changes model checkpoint weights; a tokenizer artifact does not prove it occurred.
A versioned record connecting source provenance, study activity, tests, evaluation, and an honest completion state.
